lessons.title: Food Chains, Food Webs and Ecological Pyramids
lessons.notes_html:
Producers and the Sun

The Sun is the main (ultimate) source of energy for life on the Earth. Green plants, called producers, trap the Sun's energy as chemical energy by photosynthesis and make food. All consumers — herbivores, carnivores and decomposers — depend directly or indirectly on this food.

Trophic Levels

The feeding level of an organism in an ecosystem is called its trophic level. Producers form the first trophic level, primary consumers (herbivores) the second, secondary consumers the third, and so on. Energy flows from producers to consumers through food chains and food webs.

Food Chain and Food Web

A food chain is a single, straight sequence showing who eats whom, e.g. Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake. A food web is the network formed when all the food chains of an ecosystem are joined together; in a food web one organism may be eaten by several others and may eat several kinds of food, so the feeding relationships are interlinked and more stable.

Ecological Pyramids

An ecological pyramid is the graphical representation of the trophic relationship of organisms in an ecosystem. It shows the number of organisms, biomass or energy at each trophic level. Producers occupy the base of the pyramid because they are the first trophic level: they make their own food by trapping the Sun's energy and all other organisms depend on them. They are the most numerous and contain the greatest amount of energy and biomass, while only a part of the energy passes to each next level, so the pyramid is broad at the base and narrows towards the apex.

Key Points

  • The Sun is the ultimate source of energy; producers trap it as chemical energy.
  • A trophic level is the feeding level of an organism in an ecosystem.
  • All food chains joined together form a food web.
  • Producers form the broad base of every ecological pyramid.

mcqs.q: The feeding level of an organism in an ecosystem is called:
mcqs.why: The trophic level is the feeding level of an organism — producers are the first trophic level, herbivores the second, and so on.

mcqs.q: All the food chains of an ecosystem joined together form a:
mcqs.why: A food web is the interlinked network formed when all the food chains of an ecosystem are joined together.

mcqs.q: The graphical representation of the trophic relationship of organisms in an ecosystem is called:
mcqs.why: An ecological pyramid graphically shows the number of organisms, biomass or energy at each trophic level.

mcqs.q: The energy of the Sun is trapped as chemical energy by:
mcqs.why: Green plants (producers) trap sunlight by photosynthesis and store it as chemical energy in food.

mcqs.q: Which sequence is a correct food chain?
mcqs.why: A food chain starts with a producer (grass), then a herbivore (grasshopper), then its predators (frog, then snake).

mcqs.q: Why do producers occupy the base of the ecological pyramid?
options: They depend on consumers for food
They are eaten by no organism
They make food and all other organisms depend on them
mcqs.why: Producers are the first trophic level; they contain the greatest energy and biomass, and every consumer depends on them directly or indirectly.

mcqs.q: What happens to energy as it passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: Only a part of it passes to the next level
mcqs.why: Only a part of the energy passes upward at each level, so the pyramid narrows from the broad producer base to the apex.

mcqs.q: The Sun is the main source of energy for life on Earth because:
options: it warms the soil directly for all animals
producers trap its energy by photosynthesis and all consumers depend on that food
it produces rain for the plants
it kills harmful germs in the air
mcqs.why: Producers convert sunlight into food energy; herbivores, carnivores and decomposers all depend on this food, so nearly all life runs on solar energy.

mcqs.q: In a food web, compared with a single food chain, the feeding relationships are:
mcqs.why: In a food web an organism may eat several foods and be eaten by several predators, so the relationships are interlinked and the ecosystem is more stable.

mcqs.q: In the ecological pyramid, the narrow top (apex) is occupied by:
mcqs.why: The pyramid has producers at the broad base and the top consumers (highest trophic level) at the narrow apex.

lessons.title: Ecological Relationships: Predation and Symbiosis
lessons.notes_html:
Predation

Predation is an ecological relationship in which one organism (the predator) actively hunts, kills and eats another organism (the prey). For example, a lion hunting a deer, or a frog catching an insect. Consumers that actively hunt other organisms are called predators.

Symbiosis

A relationship in which two species live together closely is called symbiosis. The organisms living together in this way are called symbionts. Symbiosis is different from predation, where one organism hunts and kills the other, and from competition, where organisms struggle for the same food or space.

Effect of Changing Populations

If the population of one species in an ecosystem is affected, the whole food web is disturbed. For example, if frogs decrease, the insects they eat will increase and damage crops, while snakes that eat frogs will decrease for lack of food. In this way a change in one population affects the resources and balance of all other populations.

Key Points

  • A predator actively hunts, kills and eats its prey.
  • Symbiosis means two species living together closely.
  • A change in one population disturbs the whole food web.

mcqs.q: Consumers that actively hunt other organisms are called:
mcqs.why: A predator is the consumer that actively hunts, kills and eats other organisms; the hunted organism is the prey.

mcqs.q: A relationship in which two species live together closely is called:
mcqs.why: Symbiosis is the close living relationship between two species; predation and competition are different kinds of relationships.

mcqs.q: In predation, the organism that is hunted and eaten is called the:
mcqs.why: The prey is the organism hunted, killed and eaten by the predator, e.g. the deer hunted by a lion.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of predation?
options: Animals competing for the same grass
mcqs.why: The frog (predator) actively hunts and eats the insect (prey) — this is predation, like a lion hunting a deer.

mcqs.q: If the population of frogs in an ecosystem decreases, what will happen first?
options: Insects will increase and snakes will decrease
mcqs.why: Frogs eat insects, so fewer frogs means more insects; snakes eat frogs, so fewer frogs means less food for snakes and their number falls.

mcqs.q: Overhunting of predators in an area will most likely cause:
options: the prey population to increase too much
the prey population to disappear at once
more producers to grow in one day
mcqs.why: If predators are overhunted, the prey population increases too much and overgrazes the plants, causing ecological imbalance.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows a predator and its prey?
options: Frog and snake only as symbionts
mcqs.why: The lion actively hunts, kills and eats the deer — the book's own example of predator and prey.

mcqs.q: A change in the population of one species affects the whole ecosystem because:
options: species are linked through food webs
only producers matter in an ecosystem
mcqs.why: Through food webs every population is linked to others, so a change in one affects the food and balance of many others.

mcqs.q: Symbiosis differs from predation because in symbiosis:
options: one organism always kills the other
organisms struggle for the same food
mcqs.why: Symbiosis is defined by two species living together closely, while in predation one organism hunts and kills the other.

mcqs.q: If a plant species in an ecosystem decreases, the herbivores depending on it will:
options: starve, and their predators will also suffer
mcqs.why: Herbivores lose their food and starve; the predators that eat those herbivores then also suffer — the whole food web is disturbed.

lessons.title: The Carbon and Oxygen Cycles
lessons.notes_html:
Two Complementary Cycles

The carbon cycle and the oxygen cycle are complementary processes that keep the balance of both gases on the Earth. Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, while respiration uses oxygen and releases carbon dioxide.

The Oxygen Cycle

Oxygen is released into the air by plants during photosynthesis and is taken up by animals and plants during respiration and by combustion. This keeps the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere balanced.

The Carbon Cycle

Carbon (as carbon dioxide) is taken up by plants for photosynthesis and is returned to the air by respiration, decomposition and the burning of fossil fuels.

Why the Cycles Matter

Because of these cycles, the amounts of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the air stay balanced: living things get oxygen to breathe and plants get carbon dioxide to make food, so life continues smoothly in the environment. Photosynthesis does not lead to global warming — it removes carbon dioxide from the air. Global warming is increased by the greenhouse effect, deforestation and burning of fossil fuels.

Key Points

  • Photosynthesis takes in CO2 and releases O2; respiration does the reverse.
  • The carbon and oxygen cycles together keep both gases balanced in the air.
  • Combustion and decomposition return carbon dioxide to the air.

mcqs.q: Which phenomenon does NOT lead to global warming?
mcqs.why: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air and releases oxygen, so it works against global warming; the other three increase it.

mcqs.q: Oxygen is released into the air by plants during:
mcqs.why: During photosynthesis plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: Carbon dioxide is returned to the air by:
options: respiration, decomposition and burning of fossil fuels
mcqs.why: Respiration, decomposition of dead bodies and combustion of fossil fuels all release carbon dioxide back into the air.

mcqs.q: The carbon and oxygen cycles are called complementary because:
options: photosynthesis uses CO2 and releases O2 while respiration uses O2 and releases CO2
oxygen is changed into carbon in them
mcqs.why: The two main processes work in opposite directions, so together they keep the amounts of both gases balanced on Earth.

mcqs.q: In the carbon cycle, plants take up carbon from the air in the form of:
mcqs.why: Plants absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis; this is how carbon leaves the air and enters living bodies as food.

mcqs.q: Combustion (burning) affects the oxygen cycle because it:
options: takes up oxygen and releases carbon dioxide
mcqs.why: Burning uses oxygen from the air and produces carbon dioxide, linking the oxygen and carbon cycles.

mcqs.q: If there were no photosynthesis on Earth, the amount of oxygen in the air would:
options: gradually decrease as respiration and burning use it up
mcqs.why: Photosynthesis is the process that releases oxygen; respiration and combustion only consume it, so the balance would be lost.

mcqs.q: The amounts of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the air stay balanced mainly because of:
options: the carbon and oxygen cycles working together
mcqs.why: The complementary carbon and oxygen cycles keep both gases balanced, so animals get oxygen and plants get carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Deforestation increases global warming because:
options: trees release carbon dioxide at night only
fewer trees means less carbon dioxide is absorbed by photosynthesis
mcqs.why: With fewer plants, less CO2 is removed from the air, so the greenhouse gas builds up and the Earth warms.

mcqs.q: Which process takes place in both plants and animals and releases carbon dioxide?
mcqs.why: All living things respire: they use oxygen and release carbon dioxide, returning carbon to the air.

lessons.title: Environmental Problems and Ecological Imbalance
lessons.notes_html:
Ecological Imbalance

Ecological imbalance is caused by factors such as overpopulation, overhunting, migration and introduction of a new population, deforestation, pollution, burning of fossil fuels, and changes in the water supply of an ecosystem.

Effects of Overhunting

Overhunting reduces the population of the hunted species and may make it endangered or extinct. If predators are overhunted, the prey population increases too much and overgrazes the plants; if a prey species is overhunted, its predators starve. Thus overhunting causes ecological imbalance and loss of biodiversity.

If Global Warming Is Not Reduced

The temperature of the Earth will keep increasing. Glaciers and polar ice will melt, sea levels will rise and coastal areas will flood; weather patterns will change, causing droughts, floods and storms; many species will die and crops will fail. So we must reduce the burning of fossil fuels, stop deforestation and control overpopulation.

Solutions of Environmental Problems

  • Reducing pollution of air, water and land.
  • Plantation — planting more and more trees; trees absorb carbon dioxide, release oxygen, reduce air pollution and global warming, and provide homes to endangered species.
  • Protection of endangered species so that food webs stay balanced.

Growing even one plant in an earthen pot helps: the plant absorbs carbon dioxide — the main greenhouse and pollutant gas — and releases fresh oxygen, traps dust on its leaves, reduces noise and keeps the surroundings cool.

Key Points

  • Overpopulation, overhunting, deforestation and pollution cause ecological imbalance.
  • Plantation, reducing pollution and protecting endangered species are the main solutions.
  • Uncontrolled global warming melts ice, raises sea levels and destroys crops and species.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a solution of environmental problems?
mcqs.why: Plantation — planting more and more trees — is one of the book's three solutions, along with reducing pollution and protecting endangered species; the other options are causes of the problems.

mcqs.q: Which of the following causes ecological imbalance?
mcqs.why: Overpopulation is listed in the book among the causes of ecological imbalance, together with overhunting and migration; the other options are solutions, not causes.

mcqs.q: Plantation helps the environment because trees:
options: absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen
increase the burning of fossil fuels
mcqs.why: Trees take in the main greenhouse gas, carbon dioxide, and release oxygen, reducing air pollution and global warming.

mcqs.q: If we do not work to reduce global warming, glaciers and polar ice will:
options: melt, raising sea levels and flooding coastal areas
move towards the equator as ice
mcqs.why: Rising temperatures melt glaciers and polar ice; the extra water raises sea levels and floods coastal areas.

mcqs.q: Overhunting a prey species will cause its predators to:
mcqs.why: Predators depend on the prey for food; if the prey is overhunted, the predators go hungry and their population falls.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a factor causing ecological imbalance?
options: changes in the water supply of an ecosystem
mcqs.why: The book lists changes in water supply, along with deforestation, pollution and burning of fossil fuels, as causes of imbalance; the other options protect the balance.

mcqs.q: A plant grown in an earthen pot reduces pollution because it:
options: uses the soil of the pot
absorbs carbon dioxide, releases oxygen and traps dust on its leaves
stops noise completely in a city
mcqs.why: By photosynthesis the plant cleans the air of the main pollutant gas and its leaves trap dust particles, keeping the surroundings fresh.

mcqs.q: Loss of biodiversity is caused by:
options: overhunting making species endangered or extinct
mcqs.why: Overhunting reduces populations and can make species endangered or extinct, which is a direct loss of biodiversity.

mcqs.q: To reduce global warming we must:
options: reduce burning of fossil fuels, stop deforestation and control overpopulation
mcqs.why: These are the steps named in the book to stop the Earth's temperature from rising further.

mcqs.q: Uncontrolled global warming will change weather patterns, causing:
options: droughts, floods and storms, and crop failures
mcqs.why: The book warns that rising temperatures disturb weather, bringing droughts, floods and storms, killing species and failing crops.

lessons.title: The Neuron and Types of Neurons
lessons.notes_html:
The Neuron

The neuron (nerve cell) is the unit of the nervous system. It consists of dendrites — the branched parts which receive messages, a cell body containing the cytoplasm and nucleus, and an axon — the long fibre which carries the message away from the cell body. The axon is covered by an insulating myelin sheath, and its branched ends, the axon terminals, pass the message to the next neuron or effector.

Neuron and Nerve

A neuron is a single nerve cell which carries nerve impulses. A nerve is a bundle of many axons present side by side and enclosed in a common sheath, which carries messages to and from the central nervous system.

Three Types of Neurons

  • Sensory neurons carry messages (impulses) from the receptors/sense organs towards the brain and spinal cord.
  • Inter-neurons in the brain and spinal cord link sensory and motor neurons and decide about the action for a certain stimulus.
  • Motor neurons carry messages from the brain and spinal cord to the effectors (muscles and glands) to produce a response.

Receptors and Effectors

Receptors are the cells or sense organs (in the eyes, ears, skin, nose and tongue) which receive stimuli from the environment and generate nerve impulses. Effectors are the parts which produce the response — the muscles and glands, which act on the orders received from the central nervous system. In short, receptors receive the message and effectors act upon it.

Key Points

  • Dendrites receive messages; the axon carries them away from the cell body.
  • Many axons enclosed in a common sheath form a nerve.
  • Sensory neurons carry messages to the CNS; motor neurons carry orders to effectors.
  • Inter-neurons decide the action for a stimulus.

mcqs.q: The parts of a neuron which receive messages are the:
mcqs.why: Dendrites are the branched parts of the neuron that receive messages and pass them to the cell body.

mcqs.q: Many axons present side by side and enclosed in a common sheath form a:
mcqs.why: A nerve is a bundle of many axons lying side by side inside a common sheath; a single cell is a neuron.

mcqs.q: Sensory neurons carry messages towards the:
mcqs.why: Sensory neurons carry impulses from the receptors/sense organs to the brain and spinal cord (the CNS).

mcqs.q: The neurons which decide about the action for a certain stimulus are:
mcqs.why: Inter-neurons, located in the brain and spinal cord, link sensory and motor neurons and decide the response to a stimulus.

mcqs.q: Motor neurons carry messages from the brain and spinal cord to the:
mcqs.why: Motor neurons deliver the CNS orders to the effectors — muscles and glands — which produce the response.

mcqs.q: The insulating covering over the axon of a neuron is called the:
mcqs.why: The myelin sheath is the insulating covering over the axon, with nodes between its segments.

mcqs.q: Receptors differ from effectors because receptors:
options: receive stimuli and generate nerve impulses
are found only in the spinal cord
mcqs.why: Receptors (in eyes, ears, skin, nose, tongue) receive stimuli and generate impulses; effectors — muscles and glands — act on the orders.

mcqs.q: The long fibre that carries the message away from the cell body is the:
mcqs.why: The axon is the long fibre carrying the impulse away from the cell body towards the axon terminals.

mcqs.q: A neuron differs from a nerve because a neuron is:
options: not part of the nervous system
mcqs.why: A neuron is one nerve cell (dendrites, cell body, axon); a nerve is a bundle of many axons in a common sheath.

mcqs.q: When you have a toothache, you feel pain because:
options: there is a cavity in your tooth
tiny bits of food are left between your teeth
bacteria digest the food and produce an acid
the cavity reaches the nerves and the nerves send a message to the brain
mcqs.why: Pain is felt only when the cavity reaches the nerves in the tooth and sensory neurons carry the message to the brain.

lessons.title: The Brain: Parts and Their Functions
lessons.notes_html:
The Cerebrum

The cerebrum is the largest part of the forebrain. It controls voluntary actions, thinking, intelligence, memory, speech and the senses. Brushing your teeth and eating breakfast are voluntary actions controlled by the cerebrum.

Hypothalamus and Midbrain

The hypothalamus, a part of the forebrain, controls body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep. The midbrain connects the forebrain with the hindbrain and controls some reflex movements of the eyes and ears, e.g. movement of the eyeballs and hearing reflexes.

Cerebellum and Medulla Oblongata

The cerebellum (hindbrain) coordinates the movements of muscles and is involved in precise and accurate body movements and in balancing the body. The medulla oblongata (hindbrain) controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat and breathing — taking a deep breath is controlled by it.

Which Part Controls Each Activity?

  • Sleeping — Forebrain (hypothalamus controls sleep).
  • Brushing teeth, eating breakfast — Forebrain (cerebrum: voluntary actions).
  • Balancing the body — Hindbrain (cerebellum).
  • Taking a deep breath — Hindbrain (medulla oblongata).

Key Points

  • The cerebrum controls thinking, memory, speech and voluntary actions.
  • The hypothalamus controls temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep.
  • The cerebellum keeps balance and makes movements precise.
  • The medulla oblongata controls heartbeat and breathing.

mcqs.q: Heartbeat is controlled by the:
mcqs.why: The medulla oblongata, a part of the hindbrain, controls involuntary actions like heartbeat and breathing.

mcqs.q: Which part of the brain is involved in precise and accurate body movements?
mcqs.why: The cerebellum coordinates muscle movements, making them precise and accurate, and maintains the balance of the body.

mcqs.q: The hypothalamus controls:
options: body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep
mcqs.why: The hypothalamus is the forebrain part that regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep.

mcqs.q: The midbrain connects the forebrain with the hindbrain and controls:
options: reflex movements of the eyes and ears
mcqs.why: The midbrain links forebrain and hindbrain and controls reflexes such as movement of the eyeballs and hearing reflexes.

mcqs.q: Balancing your body while walking is controlled by the:
mcqs.why: Balance and precise movements are the job of the cerebellum, which lies in the hindbrain.

mcqs.q: Sleeping is controlled through the:
mcqs.why: The hypothalamus — part of the forebrain — controls sleep along with temperature, hunger and thirst.

mcqs.q: The largest part of the brain, controlling thinking, memory and speech, is the:
mcqs.why: The cerebrum is the largest part of the forebrain and the seat of thinking, intelligence, memory, speech and the senses.

mcqs.q: Taking a deep breath is controlled by the:
mcqs.why: Breathing is an involuntary action controlled by the medulla oblongata in the hindbrain.

mcqs.q: Brushing your teeth is a voluntary action controlled by the:
mcqs.why: Voluntary movements like brushing teeth are planned and controlled by the cerebrum.

mcqs.q: The cerebrum differs from the cerebellum because the cerebrum:
options: maintains the balance of the body
controls voluntary actions, thinking and memory
connects the brain to the spinal cord
mcqs.why: The cerebrum controls voluntary actions, thinking, intelligence, memory, speech and senses; balance and coordination belong to the cerebellum.

lessons.title: The Central Nervous System and Reflex Action
lessons.notes_html:
The Central Nervous System (CNS)

The central nervous system consists of the brain and the spinal cord. It receives messages from all parts of the body through sensory neurons, decides about the action for a stimulus through inter-neurons, and sends orders through motor neurons to the muscles and glands. The network of nerves connecting the CNS to all body parts forms the peripheral nervous system.

Functions of the Spinal Cord

The spinal cord carries messages between the brain and the rest of the body, and it is also the centre of reflex actions, giving quick involuntary responses without involving the brain.

How a Response Is Produced

Stimulus → receptors receive it → sensory neurons carry the impulse to the CNS → inter-neurons decide the action → motor neurons carry orders to effectors → muscles or glands produce the response. The listening-and-writing activity in the book's project shows this whole chain: ears receive, nerves carry, the brain stores it as memory (a cerebrum function), and hand muscles respond by writing.

Key Points

  • The CNS is made of the brain and the spinal cord.
  • The spinal cord links the brain with the body and controls reflex actions.
  • Nerves connecting the CNS to the body form the peripheral nervous system.

mcqs.q: The central nervous system consists of the:
mcqs.why: The CNS is made of the brain and spinal cord only; the nerves spreading from them form the peripheral nervous system.

mcqs.q: The spinal cord is the centre of:
mcqs.why: Besides carrying messages to and from the brain, the spinal cord controls quick involuntary reflex actions without involving the brain.

mcqs.q: The network of nerves connecting the CNS to all body parts is called the:
mcqs.why: All the nerves linking the brain and spinal cord with the rest of the body together form the peripheral nervous system.

mcqs.q: In the CNS, the decision about the action for a stimulus is taken by:
mcqs.why: Inter-neurons inside the brain and spinal cord receive the sensory message and decide the response, then pass orders to motor neurons.

mcqs.q: The spinal cord carries messages:
options: only from the body to the brain
only from the brain to the body
between the brain and the rest of the body
mcqs.why: The spinal cord is the two-way link between the brain and the body, carrying impulses in both directions.

mcqs.q: Memory — tested when students write a paragraph they have only heard — is a function of the:
mcqs.why: Memory is stored and processed in the cerebrum; the closer the written paragraph is to the heard one, the stronger the memory.

mcqs.q: The correct order of a nervous response is:
options: receptor → sensory neuron → CNS → motor neuron → effector
mcqs.why: Receptors receive the stimulus, sensory neurons carry it to the CNS, which decides, and motor neurons order the effectors to respond.

mcqs.q: Reflex actions are quick and involuntary because they:
options: are controlled by the spinal cord without involving the brain
are produced by the sense organs alone
mcqs.why: The spinal cord gives immediate reflex responses on its own, which saves time in emergencies.

mcqs.q: Which of these is controlled by the brain rather than the spinal cord?
options: A reflex jerk of the leg
A quick pull of the hand from a hot object
mcqs.why: Thinking, intelligence, memory and speech are functions of the cerebrum in the brain; the spinal cord handles reflexes and message carrying.

mcqs.q: The brain controls which of the following?
options: thinking, memory, voluntary and many involuntary actions
mcqs.why: The brain is the master control centre: it handles thought and memory, voluntary actions, and many involuntary actions like heartbeat and breathing.

lessons.title: Protecting the Nervous System
lessons.notes_html:
Why the Brain Must Be Protected

The brain is the most important part of the nervous system — it controls thinking, memory and all body actions. A head injury can damage the brain or skull and may cause memory loss, paralysis or even death. That is why a motor cyclist is advised to wear a helmet: it acts as a protective covering for the brain in case of an accident.

Loss of Memory After an Accident

If a person cannot remember even his own name after a car accident, his head was probably injured and the cerebrum damaged. Memory, thinking and intelligence are seated in the cerebrum, so damage to it can cause loss of memory (amnesia).

If a Nerve Connection Breaks

If a nerve connection breaks, impulses cannot pass between the body part and the brain/spinal cord. The sense organ of that part cannot send sensations to the brain, and the muscles cannot receive orders, so the part may become numb and paralysed (unable to move or feel). Reflex actions of that part also stop until the connection is repaired.

Key Points

  • A helmet protects the skull and brain from injury in an accident.
  • Damage to the cerebrum can cause loss of memory.
  • A broken nerve connection makes the part numb and paralysed.

mcqs.q: A motor cyclist is advised to wear a helmet because it:
options: protects the head and brain in an accident
mcqs.why: The helmet is a protective covering for the brain — the control centre whose injury can cause memory loss, paralysis or death.

mcqs.q: A man who forgets even his name after a car accident has most likely damaged his:
mcqs.why: Memory, thinking and intelligence are seated in the cerebrum; its damage causes amnesia — loss of memory.

mcqs.q: If a nerve connection to a body part breaks, that part may become:
options: controlled directly by the sense organs
mcqs.why: With the connection broken, sensations cannot reach the brain and orders cannot reach the muscles, so the part can neither feel nor move.

mcqs.q: Memory loss after a head injury shows that memory is stored and processed in the:
mcqs.why: The cerebrum of the forebrain is the seat of memory, so its injury can erase even a person's own name from memory.

mcqs.q: A serious head injury is dangerous because it can cause:
options: memory loss, paralysis or even death
mcqs.why: The brain controls all body actions; damage to it can destroy memory, paralyse parts of the body, or prove fatal.

mcqs.q: When a nerve connection breaks, reflex actions of that part:
options: also stop until the connection is repaired
shift to the other side of the body
are taken over by the skin
mcqs.why: Reflexes need an unbroken path through the neurons; a break stops sensations, movements and reflexes of that part.

mcqs.q: The part of the nervous system that must be protected most carefully is the:
mcqs.why: The brain controls thinking, memory and every body action, so protecting it — for example with a helmet — is essential.

mcqs.q: Paralysis of a limb means the limb:
options: cannot move or feel because its nerve connection is damaged
mcqs.why: When impulses cannot pass between the limb and the CNS, the muscles get no orders and the senses send no messages — the limb is paralysed.

mcqs.q: Which safety habit directly protects the nervous system?
options: Wearing a helmet while riding a motorcycle
mcqs.why: The helmet guards the skull and brain against the injuries that cause memory loss, paralysis or death.

mcqs.q: Amnesia (loss of memory) after an accident is related to damage of the:
options: part of the brain that stores memory — the cerebrum
mcqs.why: The accident case in the book is explained by cerebrum damage: memory is a cerebrum function, so the man forgot his own name.

chapters.title: Unit 3 — Variation, Heredity and Cell Division

lessons.title: Variation and Adaptation
lessons.notes_html:
Variation

The differences found among the individuals of the same species are called variation — for example, differences in height, eye colour and blood group among brothers and sisters. A mark of a cut on the skin is not a genetic variation, because it is acquired during life and is not controlled by genes.

Source of Genetic Variation

The primary source of genetic variation is the changes (mutations) in the genes and the new combinations of genes formed during meiosis (crossing over and independent assortment) and fertilisation, when genes from two parents combine in the offspring. That is why offspring differ from their parents and from each other.

Adaptation

An adaptation is a special character (structural or behavioural) that helps an organism to survive and reproduce in its specific environment. Variations occur in individuals and may or may not help survival, while adaptations are characters developed for a particular environment over generations.

Examples of Adaptation

  • Cactus (desert): leaves changed into spines to reduce water loss; thick stem stores water.
  • Lotus/water lily (water): broad floating leaves and air spaces in stems to float and breathe.
  • Pine (cold hills): needle-like leaves and cone shape so snow slides off easily.
  • Fish (water): streamlined body, fins for swimming and balance, gills to absorb dissolved oxygen, scales and slimy skin for protection, and a swim bladder to float at different depths.

Key Points

  • Variation = differences among individuals of the same species.
  • Mutations and new gene combinations in meiosis and fertilisation cause genetic variation.
  • Adaptations help an organism survive in its particular environment.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a genetic variation?
options: Mark of a cut on skin
mcqs.why: A cut mark is acquired during life and is not controlled by genes, while eye colour, earlobes and blood group are inherited genetic characters.

mcqs.q: You are different from your brothers and sisters. This is called:
mcqs.why: The differences among individuals of the same species — even among siblings — are called variation.

the effect of weather on the skin

is found in only one individual for one day
mcqs.why: Adaptations such as the spines of a cactus or the fins of a fish are developed for a particular environment and aid survival.

mcqs.q: The cactus is adapted to the desert because:

its leaves are changed into spines and its thick stem stores water

mcqs.q: Fish absorb dissolved oxygen from water through their:

mcqs.q: The pine tree of cold hilly areas has needle-like leaves and a cone shape so that:
mcqs.why: The cone shape and needle leaves let snow slide off without breaking the branches — an adaptation to cold hilly areas.

mcqs.q: Variation differs from adaptation because variation:
options: occurs in individuals and may or may not help survival
is developed only for one environment
mcqs.why: Variations are individual differences that may or may not be useful; adaptations are characters developed over generations for a specific environment.

mcqs.q: Aquatic plants like the lotus float and breathe in water because they have:
options: broad floating leaves and air spaces in their stems
mcqs.why: Broad leaves float on the surface and air spaces in the stems keep the plant buoyant and supplied with air.

mcqs.why: A streamlined body offers little resistance in water, and with fins for balance and direction the fish swims efficiently.

lessons.title: Genes, DNA and Heredity
lessons.notes_html:
Genes and Chromosomes

A gene is a section (part) of DNA which has the information for making a specific protein. Genes are located on the chromosomes and control the hereditary characters of an organism, e.g. the gene for eye colour. Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins. In humans, eye colour is developed due to the effects of genes.

Structure of DNA

DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) has a double helix structure, like a twisted ladder. It is made of two long strands of nucleotides; each nucleotide consists of a sugar (deoxyribose), a phosphate group and a nitrogen base. There are four bases: Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Cytosine (C) and Guanine (G). The sugar-phosphate strands form the sides of the ladder and the base pairs form its steps: A always pairs with T and C with G. The specific sequence of these bases stores the genetic information. In the book's model project, two coloured paper strips form the strands and toothpicks joining them represent the base pairs.

Heredity

Heredity is the transfer of characters (traits) from parents to their offspring through genes. The characters which are passed from parents to offspring are called hereditary characters. During reproduction the gametes carry the genes of both parents to the zygote, so the offspring resembles its parents while also showing variations. Heredity maintains the continuity of species from generation to generation.

Key Points

  • A gene is a section of DNA carrying information for a specific protein.
  • Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins.
  • In DNA, A pairs with T and C pairs with G.
  • Heredity transfers characters from parents to offspring through genes.

mcqs.q: In humans, eye colour is developed due to the effects of:
mcqs.why: Eye colour is a hereditary character controlled by genes located on the chromosomes.

mcqs.q: The section of DNA which has information for making a specific protein is called a:
mcqs.why: A gene is the part of DNA that carries the coded information for making one specific protein.

mcqs.q: Chromosomes are made of:
mcqs.why: Chromosomes consist of DNA wound around proteins; fats are not a part of chromosomes.

mcqs.q: The characters which are passed from parents to offspring are called:
mcqs.why: Characters transferred through genes from parents to offspring — like eye colour and blood group — are hereditary characters.

mcqs.q: DNA has a double helix structure like a twisted ladder. Its steps are formed by:
mcqs.why: The two sugar-phosphate strands form the sides of the ladder and the base pairs (A–T and C–G) form its steps.

mcqs.q: In DNA, adenine (A) always pairs with:
mcqs.why: Base pairing in DNA is fixed: A pairs with T and C pairs with G.

mcqs.q: Each nucleotide of DNA consists of:
options: a sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogen base
mcqs.why: A nucleotide = deoxyribose sugar + phosphate group + one of the four bases A, T, C or G.

mcqs.q: Heredity is important because it:
options: stops all variation in a species
transfers characters from parents to offspring and maintains continuity of species
changes the chromosome number every generation
mcqs.why: Through gametes, genes of both parents reach the zygote, so offspring resemble parents and the species continues generation after generation.

mcqs.q: Genes are located on the:
mcqs.why: Genes are sections of the DNA that makes up chromosomes in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: In the book's DNA model, the toothpicks joining the two paper strips represent:
options: the base pairs (A with T, C with G)
mcqs.why: The two paper strips are the strands (backbones); the toothpicks between them are the paired bases forming the steps of the ladder.

lessons.title: Mitosis and Meiosis
lessons.notes_html:
Interphase

Before a cell divides, it passes through interphase, during which the chromosomes are duplicated, so that each daughter cell can receive a full set.

Mitosis

Mitosis takes place in somatic (body) cells. One parent cell divides into two daughter cells and the chromosome number remains the same (diploid, 46 in humans). Mitosis is responsible for growth and repair of the body.

Meiosis

Meiosis takes place in reproductive cells to form gametes. One cell divides into four daughter cells and the chromosome number is halved (haploid, 23 in humans) during meiosis-I. Meiosis is responsible for sexual reproduction and brings variation in offspring.

Reading the Figures

Chromosomes arranged on the equator as homologous pairs show a phase of meiosis (metaphase-I) — pairing happens only in meiosis. Single chromosomes (separated chromatids) moving towards opposite poles show a phase of mitosis (anaphase), keeping the chromosome number the same.

Key Points

  • Chromosomes duplicate during interphase, before division.
  • Mitosis: 2 daughter cells, chromosome number unchanged — for growth and repair.
  • Meiosis: 4 daughter cells, chromosome number halved — for gamete formation.
  • Reduction of chromosomes takes place during meiosis-I.

mcqs.q: An event that occurs during interphase is:
mcqs.why: During interphase the cell prepares for division by duplicating its chromosomes; actual division of nucleus and cytoplasm comes later.

mcqs.q: Reduction of chromosomes takes place during:
mcqs.why: In meiosis-I the homologous chromosomes separate, halving the chromosome number from diploid to haploid.

mcqs.q: Mitosis takes place in:
mcqs.why: Mitosis occurs in body cells for growth and repair, keeping the chromosome number the same (46 in humans).

mcqs.q: Meiosis produces:
options: four daughter cells with the chromosome number halved
mcqs.why: One reproductive cell divides by meiosis into four haploid gametes, each with 23 chromosomes in humans.

mcqs.q: Which division is responsible for growth and repair of the body?
mcqs.why: Mitosis makes identical new body cells with the full chromosome number, so the body grows and wounds are repaired.

mcqs.q: A figure shows chromosomes arranged on the equator as homologous pairs. This is a phase of:
mcqs.why: Homologous chromosomes pair up and arrange together on the equator only in meiosis-I; in mitosis chromosomes arrange singly.

mcqs.q: A figure shows separated chromatids moving towards opposite poles, keeping the number the same. This is:
mcqs.why: In mitotic anaphase the chromatids separate to opposite poles and the chromosome number stays unchanged — the growth/repair division.

mcqs.q: Meiosis brings variation in offspring because of:
options: crossing over and new combinations of genes
mcqs.why: Crossing over and independent assortment during meiosis reshuffle genes, so gametes — and offspring — differ from each other.

mcqs.q: After mitosis, each daughter cell in humans has:
mcqs.why: Mitosis keeps the diploid number constant: parent cell 46 → two daughter cells with 46 each.

mcqs.q: Meiosis is necessary for sexual reproduction because it:
options: forms haploid gametes so fertilisation restores the diploid number
mcqs.why: Haploid gametes (23 + 23) fuse to restore 46 in the zygote, keeping the number constant in every generation.

lessons.title: Gametes, Fertilisation and Repair of the Body
lessons.notes_html:
Haploid Gametes

Gametes (sperm and egg cells) are haploid: in humans a sperm has 23 chromosomes and an egg cell also has 23 chromosomes. A zygote is formed by the fusion of a sperm cell and an egg cell, restoring the diploid number 46.

Why Gametes Must Be Haploid

If the gametes were diploid (46 each), their fusion would produce a zygote with 92 chromosomes — double the normal number. The chromosome number would keep doubling in every generation, the genetic balance would be destroyed and the offspring would be abnormal and unable to survive. Haploid gametes keep the chromosome number constant in every generation.

Repair by Mitosis

An injury needs more and more cells for repair, and mitosis provides them: cells divide into two identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number, quickly replacing damaged and dead cells. When you get a cut on your hand, blood first clots at the wound and stops the bleeding; then the cells around the wound divide by mitosis, fill the gap, repair the tissue and form new skin over the cut. This is how wounds heal in a few days, provided the wound is kept clean from germs.

Key Points

  • Sperm and egg each carry 23 chromosomes in humans.
  • Zygote = sperm + egg; it has the full 46 chromosomes.
  • Wounds heal by mitosis producing new cells at the injured place.

mcqs.q: In humans, a sperm has 23 chromosomes. An egg cell has:
mcqs.why: Both gametes are haploid with 23 chromosomes, so their fusion restores the diploid number 46 in the zygote.

mcqs.q: A zygote is formed by the fusion of:
mcqs.why: Fertilisation is the fusion of a male gamete (sperm) with a female gamete (egg), forming the zygote.

mcqs.q: If gametes were diploid, the zygote would have:
mcqs.why: 46 + 46 = 92. The number would keep doubling each generation, destroying the genetic balance, so the offspring could not survive normally.

mcqs.q: The type of cell division that provides more cells for repair of an injury is:
mcqs.why: Mitosis produces identical new body cells with the same chromosome number, quickly replacing damaged and dead cells at the injury.

mcqs.q: When skin is cut, the wound heals because:
options: cells around the wound divide by mitosis and form new skin
mcqs.why: After the blood clots, neighbouring cells divide mitotically, fill the gap and repair the tissue with new skin.

mcqs.q: The first thing that happens when skin is cut is:
options: blood clots at the wound and stops the bleeding
mcqs.why: Clotting seals the wound first; then mitosis in the surrounding cells repairs the damage over the next few days.

mcqs.q: Gametes are haploid so that:
options: the chromosome number stays constant in every generation
mcqs.why: Haploid sperm (23) + haploid egg (23) = diploid zygote (46) — the species number is restored exactly, generation after generation.

mcqs.q: The zygote of humans contains:
mcqs.why: 23 from the sperm plus 23 from the egg gives the normal diploid number 46 in the zygote.

mcqs.q: Which cells in the human body are haploid?
mcqs.why: Only the gametes, formed by meiosis, are haploid (23); all somatic cells are diploid (46).

mcqs.q: Growth of the body from a single zygote to millions of cells takes place by:
mcqs.why: The zygote and its descendants divide by mitosis, producing more and more identical body cells for growth.

lessons.title: Genetic Engineering and Recombinant DNA
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Biotechnology?

Biotechnology is the use of living organisms (or their parts, cells and enzymes) to make useful products for mankind. In modern biotechnology, genes are transferred from one organism to another by genetic engineering to produce useful things like insulin, vaccines and improved crops.

Plasmids and Recombinant DNA

Bacteria contain, besides their main chromosome, additional small circular pieces of DNA called plasmids. Genetic engineers cut a plasmid, attach a foreign gene to it, and put it back into a bacterium. The plasmid together with the attached foreign gene is collectively called recombinant DNA, and the bacterium carrying it is used to produce the desired product.

Why Bacteria Are Used

The organisms whose cells and plasmids are usually used in genetic engineering are bacteria, because bacteria divide very fast and make colonies — so millions of copies of the inserted gene (and its product) are produced quickly and cheaply. A gene is inserted into a bacterium by genetic engineering, not by tissue culture or fermentation.

Genes

Sections of DNA serving as codes for developing characters in an organism are called genes. Transferring a gene transfers the character it codes for — for example, the human insulin gene transferred into bacteria makes the bacteria produce human insulin.

Key Points

  • Plasmids are the small circular DNA pieces in bacteria used as gene carriers.
  • Plasmid + foreign gene = recombinant DNA.
  • Bacteria are used because they divide very fast and form colonies.

mcqs.q: The additional circular pieces of DNA present in a bacterial cell are called:
mcqs.why: Plasmids are the small extra circular DNA molecules in bacteria, used by genetic engineers as carriers of foreign genes.

mcqs.q: Plasmid and the attached foreign gene with it are collectively called:
mcqs.why: When a foreign gene is joined to a plasmid, the combined DNA is called recombinant DNA.

mcqs.q: The organisms whose cells and plasmids are usually used in genetic engineering are:
mcqs.why: Bacteria are the usual hosts because they carry plasmids and multiply very fast into colonies.

mcqs.q: Sections of DNA serving as codes for developing characters in an organism are called:
mcqs.why: Genes are the DNA sections that code for the characters (proteins) of an organism.

mcqs.q: Genetic engineers use bacteria in genetic engineering because:
options: their nucleus is very big and easy to handle
bacteria divide very fast and make colonies
their chromosome is made of DNA and proteins
mcqs.why: Rapid division means the inserted gene is copied into millions of bacteria quickly, producing the desired product in large amounts.

mcqs.q: A gene is inserted into a bacterium by:
mcqs.why: Inserting a foreign gene into a bacterium's plasmid is the basic technique of genetic engineering.

mcqs.q: Biotechnology is best defined as:
options: the use of living organisms or their parts to make useful products for mankind
the making of machines for factories
the classification of animals and plants
mcqs.why: Biotechnology uses living organisms, cells and enzymes to produce useful products such as insulin, vaccines and improved crops.

mcqs.q: In recombinant DNA technology, the plasmid acts as a:
options: carrier (vector) of the foreign gene into the bacterium
mcqs.why: The foreign gene is attached to the plasmid, and the plasmid carries it into the bacterial cell, where it is copied with the plasmid.

mcqs.q: When the human insulin gene is put into bacteria, the bacteria:
mcqs.why: The transferred gene codes for insulin, so the engineered bacteria manufacture human insulin in large quantities.

mcqs.q: Which feature makes plasmids suitable for genetic engineering?
options: They are small circular DNA pieces that can carry a foreign gene
They are made of proteins only
They are found only in viruses
mcqs.why: Because plasmids are small and separate from the main chromosome, a gene can be joined to them and carried into bacteria.

lessons.title: Products of Biotechnology
lessons.notes_html:
Life-Saving Products

  • Insulin — produced by genetically engineered bacteria for diabetic patients. Genetic engineers get insulin by inserting the insulin gene into bacteria, not by taking it from the human pancreas.
  • Interferon — used against viral diseases and cancer.
  • Beta-endorphin — a pain-relieving product of biotechnology.
  • Vaccines and antibiotics (like penicillin) — protect and cure millions of people.

Quinine is not a biotechnology product — it is obtained naturally from the bark of the cinchona tree.

How Biotechnology Has Changed Health

Human insulin is now produced in bacteria in large quantities instead of depending on animal pancreas; vaccines protect against many diseases; interferon is used against viruses and cancer; antibiotics are produced by microorganisms on a large scale; and genetic engineering is developing gene therapy for hereditary diseases, along with test kits to diagnose diseases quickly. Diseases that were once incurable can now be treated or prevented.

Vaccines in History

Smallpox — a deadly pandemic disease — was controlled and finally eradicated from the world by the smallpox vaccine (WHO declared eradication in 1980). Polio has been controlled in almost all countries through the polio vaccine, and the COVID-19 pandemic was controlled largely through vaccines.

Key Points

  • Insulin for diabetics is made by bacteria carrying the human insulin gene.
  • Interferon is used against viral diseases and cancer.
  • Quinine is a natural plant product, not a biotechnology product.
  • Vaccines eradicated smallpox and have nearly eradicated polio.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a biotechnology product?
mcqs.why: Quinine is obtained naturally from cinchona bark; insulin, beta-endorphin and interferon are produced through biotechnology.

mcqs.q: Genetic engineers get insulin for diabetic patients by:
options: isolating it from the human pancreas
isolating it from the pancreas of other animals
inserting the insulin gene in the human pancreas
inserting the insulin gene in bacteria
mcqs.why: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria, which then produce human insulin in large quantities.

mcqs.q: Interferon is a biotechnology product used against:
mcqs.why: Interferon is one of the life-saving biotechnology products, used in the treatment of viral diseases and cancer.

mcqs.q: Two life-saving products of biotechnology are:
mcqs.why: Insulin (for diabetics) and interferon (against viruses and cancer) are named in the book as life-saving biotechnology products.

mcqs.q: The pandemic disease eradicated from the world by a vaccine is:
mcqs.why: The smallpox vaccine controlled the disease so completely that WHO declared it eradicated in 1980.

mcqs.q: Before genetic engineering, insulin for patients was limited because it depended on:
mcqs.why: Insulin was taken from animal pancreas in small amounts; engineered bacteria now produce it in bulk.

mcqs.q: Antibiotics such as penicillin are produced by:
mcqs.why: Penicillin is produced from a fungus (Penicillium); biotechnology grows such microorganisms on a large scale to make antibiotics.

mcqs.q: Gene therapy, being developed through genetic engineering, aims to treat:
mcqs.why: Gene therapy tries to correct the faulty genes that cause hereditary diseases — a new branch of biotechnology in health.

mcqs.q: Polio has been controlled in almost all countries through:
mcqs.why: Vaccination campaigns with the polio vaccine have controlled polio nearly all over the world, including Pakistan's near-eradication.

mcqs.q: Biotechnology helps in diagnosing diseases quickly by making:
mcqs.why: Biotechnology produces diagnostic test kits that detect diseases quickly, along with medicines and vaccines.

lessons.title: Applications of Biotechnology
lessons.notes_html:
In Agriculture

Biotechnology produces genetically modified crops which are resistant to diseases and insect pests (so less pesticide is needed), resistant to herbicides, higher yielding, and improved in nutritional quality — e.g. Bt cotton. It also produces crops that can grow in difficult conditions like salty or dry soil. The objectives of genetic modification of plants include production of disease resistant plants, improvement in nutritional quality and production of herbicide resistant plants.

In Health

Production of life-saving medicines — insulin, interferon, beta-endorphin, vaccines and antibiotics — by genetically engineered microorganisms.

In Food Production

Fermentation by microorganisms makes bread, yogurt, cheese and other foods, and improves the quality, taste and storage life of food products.

Biotechnology in Daily Life

Products used daily include bread and naan raised by yeast, yogurt and cheese made by bacterial fermentation, vinegar and pickles, medicines such as antibiotics and insulin, vaccines given to children, washing powders containing enzymes, and improved crop varieties such as seedless grapes and Bt cotton clothing.

Great Contributors

  • Louis Pasteur (food production): discovered fermentation by microorganisms and pasteurisation, making milk and foods safe and long-lasting.
  • Alexander Fleming (medicine): discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, produced from the fungus Penicillium.
  • Norman Borlaug (agriculture): developed high-yielding, disease resistant wheat varieties — the Green Revolution.

Key Points

  • GM crops: disease resistant, herbicide resistant, higher yield, better nutrition.
  • Fermentation by microbes produces bread, yogurt and cheese.
  • Pasteur, Fleming and Borlaug are the book's model contributors in food, medicine and agriculture.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an objective of genetic modification of plants?
mcqs.why: The book's objectives for modifying plants are: disease resistant plants, herbicide resistant plants and improved nutritional quality — the other options are the opposite of these aims.

mcqs.q: Bt cotton is an example of biotechnology in:
mcqs.why: Bt cotton is a genetically modified, insect-resistant crop — an application of biotechnology in agriculture.

mcqs.q: Bread and yogurt are produced with the help of:
mcqs.why: Yeast fermentation raises bread, and bacterial fermentation turns milk into yogurt and cheese — biotechnology in food production.

mcqs.q: Genetically modified crops help farmers because they:
options: need more pesticide than normal crops
are resistant to diseases and pests, so less pesticide is needed
mcqs.why: Disease- and pest-resistant GM crops reduce losses and pesticide use while giving higher yields.

mcqs.q: Who discovered fermentation and pasteurisation, contributing to food production?
mcqs.why: Pasteur discovered that microorganisms cause fermentation and invented pasteurisation to make milk and foods safe.

mcqs.q: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by:
mcqs.why: Fleming discovered penicillin, produced from the fungus Penicillium; it has saved millions of lives.

mcqs.q: Norman Borlaug's contribution to agriculture was:
options: high-yielding, disease resistant wheat varieties (Green Revolution)
mcqs.why: Borlaug developed improved wheat varieties that greatly increased food production in countries like Pakistan and India.

mcqs.q: Washing powders that contain enzymes are an example of biotechnology in:
mcqs.why: Enzyme washing powders, fermented foods, medicines and vaccines are biotechnology products used in everyday life.

mcqs.q: Biotechnology can help crops grow in difficult conditions such as:
mcqs.why: Genetic modification can produce crops able to grow in salty or dry soils, increasing food production on poor land.

mcqs.q: Improving the nutritional quality of plants by genetic modification means:
options: increasing useful nutrients such as vitamins in the crop
mcqs.why: One objective of plant modification is better nutritional quality — crops richer in vitamins and other nutrients.

lessons.title: Periods, Groups and Atomic Number
lessons.notes_html:
The Periodic Table

The Periodic Table arranges all the elements in the increasing order of their atomic numbers. An element is a pure substance which consists of only one kind of atoms and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by ordinary chemical means. There are about 118 elements, 92 of which are naturally occurring, for example hydrogen, oxygen, iron and gold.

Periods

A period is a horizontal row of elements in the Periodic Table. There are seven periods. In a period, elements are arranged from left to right in the continuous increasing order of their atomic numbers, and a new period begins with the start of a new electron shell. So the period number tells us how many shells an atom uses: magnesium (2, 8, 2) and phosphorus are both in the 3rd period.

Groups

A group is a vertical column of elements in the Periodic Table. There are 18 groups. Groups are numbered on the basis of the number of electrons in the outermost (valence) shell, so elements of a group have similar chemical properties and are often called a family.

Atomic Number

The atomic number of an element is the number of protons present in the nucleus of its atom. It is also equal to the number of electrons in a neutral atom. Hydrogen has atomic number 1 and carbon 6. Hydrogen has only one electron, and it lies in its first and only shell, so there is 1 electron in the valence shell of H. Helium has atomic number 2, so a helium atom contains two electrons. In the second period, the fourth element is carbon, whose atomic number is 6.

Key Points

  • A period is a horizontal row; there are 7 periods in the Periodic Table.
  • A group is a vertical column; there are 18 groups.
  • Atomic number = number of protons = number of electrons in a neutral atom.
  • Elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic number.
  • A new period begins with the start of a new electron shell.

mcqs.q: An element of the third period in the Periodic Table is:
mcqs.why: Phosphorus has electronic arrangement 2, 8, 5, so its electrons occupy three shells and it lies in the third period. H and He use one shell and Li uses two.

mcqs.q: Mg belongs to which period of the Periodic Table?
mcqs.why: Magnesium has atomic number 12 and arrangement 2, 8, 2. Its electrons are in three shells, so it belongs to the 3rd period.

mcqs.q: How many periods are there in the Periodic Table?
mcqs.why: The Periodic Table has seven horizontal rows, called periods. A new period starts whenever a new electron shell begins to fill.

mcqs.q: An atom containing two electrons is:
mcqs.why: Helium has atomic number 2, and in a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the atomic number, so a helium atom contains two electrons.

mcqs.q: The atomic number of the element at the fourth position in the second period is:
mcqs.why: The second period runs Li (3), Be (4), B (5), C (6). The fourth element is carbon, so its atomic number is 6.

mcqs.q: A group in the Periodic Table is:
mcqs.why: A group is a vertical column. There are 18 groups, and elements in one group have the same number of valence electrons and similar chemical properties.

mcqs.q: The atomic number of an element is the number of:
mcqs.why: Atomic number is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus. It also equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom, which is why elements are arranged by it.

mcqs.q: How many electrons are there in the valence shell of hydrogen?
mcqs.why: Hydrogen has atomic number 1, so it has only one electron. That electron is in its first and only shell, which is its valence shell, so the answer is 1.

mcqs.q: Elements in the Periodic Table are arranged in increasing order of their:
mcqs.why: The modern Periodic Table arranges elements left to right and top to bottom in continuously increasing atomic number, starting with hydrogen at 1.

mcqs.q: Oxygen (atomic number 8, arrangement 2, 6) is located in period:
mcqs.why: Oxygen's electrons are arranged in two shells (2, 6). The number of shells used gives the period number, so oxygen is in the 2nd period.

lessons.title: Families of Elements
lessons.notes_html:
Why Groups Are Called Families

Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons, so they react in similar ways and show similar chemical properties. That is why a group is often called a family. The chemical properties of elements depend mainly on the number of electrons in their valence shell.

Alkali Metals — Group 1

The alkali metals are Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Caesium (Cs) and Francium (Fr). Each has 1 valence electron, so they are very reactive soft metals. Sodium (Na, atomic number 11, arrangement 2, 8, 1) is in group 1 and period 3.

Alkaline Earth Metals — Group 2

The alkaline earth metals are Beryllium (Be), Magnesium (Mg), Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba) and Radium (Ra). Magnesium (2, 8, 2) and calcium (2, 8, 8, 2) are in the same group because both have 2 electrons in their valence shell.

Halogens — Group 17

The halogens are Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I) and Astatine (At). Chlorine is the group 17 element among the common examples; each halogen has 7 valence electrons.

Noble Gases — Group 18

The noble gases are Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe) and Radon (Rn). Neon belongs to the noble gases. Their valence shells are complete, so they are very unreactive. Hydrogen is a special case: it is in period 1 and group 1, so its period number and group number are the same.

Key Points

  • Group 1 = alkali metals; Group 2 = alkaline earth metals.
  • Group 17 = halogens; Group 18 = noble gases.
  • Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons.
  • Similar valence electrons means similar chemical properties.
  • Mg and Ca are both in Group 2 because each has 2 valence electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an alkali metal?
mcqs.why: Sodium (Na) is in group 1 with 1 valence electron, so it is an alkali metal. F is a halogen, Be is an alkaline earth metal and Al is in group 13.

mcqs.q: Ne belongs to:
mcqs.why: Neon (Ne) is in group 18. The group 18 elements — He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn — are called the noble gases because their valence shells are complete.

mcqs.q: An element of group 17 of the Periodic Table is:
mcqs.why: Chlorine (Cl) is a halogen in group 17 with 7 valence electrons. Argon is a noble gas, sulphur is in group 16 and silicon in group 14.

mcqs.q: The halogens are the family of group:
mcqs.why: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine form group 17. They are called halogens and each has 7 electrons in its valence shell.

mcqs.q: Magnesium and calcium are placed in the same group because both have:
mcqs.why: Mg is 2, 8, 2 and Ca is 2, 8, 8, 2. Both end with 2 valence electrons, and groups are based on valence electrons, so both sit in Group 2.

mcqs.q: The chemical properties of elements in a group are similar because they have the same number of:
mcqs.why: Chemical behaviour depends mainly on the valence (outermost) shell. All elements in a group share the same number of valence electrons, so they react in similar ways.

mcqs.q: Which element has the same period number and group number?
mcqs.why: Hydrogen is in period 1 and group 1, so its period number and group number are both 1 and therefore the same.

mcqs.q: The alkaline earth metals belong to group:
mcqs.why: Beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium form group 2, the alkaline earth metals, each with 2 valence electrons.

mcqs.q: Sodium belongs to which family of metals?
mcqs.why: Sodium has 1 electron in its valence shell (2, 8, 1), placing it in group 1, the family called the alkali metals.

mcqs.q: Oxygen is located in which group of the Periodic Table?
mcqs.why: Oxygen has arrangement 2, 6, so it has 6 valence electrons and belongs to group 16. It needs 2 more electrons to complete its valence shell.

lessons.title: Metals, Non-metals and Element Profiles
lessons.notes_html:
Metals and Non-metals

Metals such as copper (Cu), sodium and iron conduct heat and electricity, are hard, shiny and can be shaped. Non-metals such as hydrogen, carbon, chlorine and oxygen do not show these properties. Hydrogen is a non-metal even though it sits in group 1.

Properties of Metals and Their Uses

  • Conductance of heat — metals conduct heat well, so they are used for cooking utensils like pots, pans and kettles.
  • Conductance of electricity — copper and aluminium are used for electric wires and cables.
  • Malleability and ductility — metals can be beaten into thin sheets and drawn into wires, so they are used for foils, sheets, jewellery and wires.
  • Hardness — hard metals like iron and steel are used for tools, machines, bridges and buildings.
  • Lustre — metals shine when polished, so gold, silver and chromium are used for jewellery, mirrors and decoration.

Mercury in Thermometers

Mercury is a metal which is liquid at room temperature. It expands uniformly on heating, does not stick to the glass wall of the thermometer, and is shiny and opaque so its level is easily seen. Its boiling point is high and freezing point low, so it works over a wide range.

Element Profiles: Sodium and Oxygen

Sodium: symbol Na, atomic number 11, period 3, group 1, an alkali metal. Oxygen: atomic number 8, group 16, period 2, a non-metal with 6 valence electrons needing 2 more to complete its shell. Oxygen is essential for respiration and is necessary for burning, for example in cooking gas, welding and rockets.

Periodic Trends (Project)

Moving left to right in a period, the atomic number increases one by one, valence electrons increase from 1 to 8, and atomic size generally decreases because the increasing nuclear charge pulls the electrons closer. Moving top to bottom in a group, valence electrons stay the same but a new shell is added at each step, so atomic size increases.

Key Points

  • Copper is a metal; hydrogen is a non-metal.
  • Metals conduct heat and electricity, and are malleable, ductile, hard and shiny.
  • Mercury is a liquid metal used in thermometers because it expands uniformly.
  • Atomic size decreases across a period and increases down a group.
  • Sodium: Na, atomic number 11, period 3, group 1.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a metal?
mcqs.why: Copper (Cu) is a metal: it conducts heat and electricity and is used for wires. Carbon and chlorine are non-metals and neon is a noble gas.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a non-metal?
mcqs.why: Hydrogen (H) is a non-metal gas, even though it is placed in group 1. Sodium, lithium and beryllium are all metals.

mcqs.q: Copper and aluminium are used for electric wires because metals:
mcqs.why: Metals are good conductors of electricity, so copper and aluminium are drawn into wires and cables for carrying electric current.

mcqs.q: The property of metals that allows them to be beaten into thin sheets is called:
mcqs.why: Malleability is the ability to be beaten into thin sheets, while ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires. Both make metals useful for foils, sheets and jewellery.

mcqs.q: Mercury is used in thermometers mainly because it:
options: Expands uniformly on heating and does not stick to glass
mcqs.why: Mercury is liquid at room temperature, expands uniformly, does not stick to the glass wall, and is shiny and opaque so its level is easy to read accurately.

mcqs.q: Iron and steel are used for tools, bridges and buildings because metals can be:
mcqs.why: Hardness is the property used here: hard metals like iron and steel can bear heavy loads, so they are chosen for tools, machines, bridges and buildings.

mcqs.q: When we move from left to right in a period, the atomic size generally:
mcqs.why: Across a period the nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell, so the pull on the electrons grows stronger and the atomic size generally decreases.

mcqs.q: When we move from top to bottom in a group, the atomic size:
mcqs.why: Down a group a new electron shell is added at each step. The atoms get bigger even though the number of valence electrons remains the same.

mcqs.q: How many electrons does an oxygen atom require to complete its valence shell?
mcqs.why: Oxygen has 6 electrons in its valence shell. It needs 2 more electrons to reach an octet of 8 and complete the shell.

mcqs.q: The symbol and atomic number of sodium are:
mcqs.why: Sodium has the symbol Na and atomic number 11, with arrangement 2, 8, 1. That places it in period 3 and group 1, among the alkali metals.

lessons.title: Chemical Reactions, Reactants and Products
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Chemical Reaction?

A chemical reaction is the process during which a substance changes into an entirely new substance with different chemical composition and properties. During a reaction, the atoms present in different substances are rearranged to form new substances.

Reactants and Products

The substances which take part in a chemical reaction are called reactants; they are written on the left side of a chemical equation. The substances formed as a result of the reaction are called products; they are written on the right side. In C + O2 → CO2, carbon and oxygen are the reactants and carbon dioxide is the product.

Chemical Equations

A chemical equation is the representation of a chemical reaction in terms of symbols, formulae and signs indicating the physical states of the substances, for example CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(g). Carbon burns in air to release energy along with the formation of carbon dioxide, and zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give zinc sulphate and hydrogen.

Signs That a Reaction Has Taken Place

  • Evolution of a gas (bubbles or fizzing)
  • Formation of a precipitate (an insoluble solid)
  • Change in colour
  • Change in temperature — heat evolved or absorbed
  • Production of light or flame, or a new smell

When a magnesium ribbon is ignited in air, it burns with a dazzling white light and forms white magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. Iron reacts with hydrochloric acid to give iron chloride and hydrogen gas: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2. Carbon dioxide and water form carbonic acid: CO2 + H2O → H2CO3, the same reaction that, with sunlight and chlorophyll, is the basis of photosynthesis.

Key Points

  • Reactants are written on the left side of an equation; products on the right side.
  • In a chemical reaction atoms are rearranged to form new substances.
  • Zinc + dilute sulphuric acid gives zinc sulphate and hydrogen.
  • Gas evolution, precipitate, colour or temperature change signal a reaction.
  • Magnesium burns in air with a dazzling white light.

mcqs.q: Carbon burns in air to release energy along with the formation of:
mcqs.why: Burning carbon follows C + O2 → CO2. Carbon combines only with oxygen, so the single product formed along with energy is carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: The products of the reaction between zinc and dilute sulphuric acid are:
mcqs.why: Zinc is an active metal and reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form the salt zinc sulphate, while hydrogen gas is released: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2.

mcqs.q: In the equation C + O2 → CO2, the reactants are:
mcqs.why: Reactants are the substances written on the left side of the arrow that take part in the reaction. Here carbon and oxygen react, and carbon dioxide is the product.

mcqs.q: A chemical reaction is a process in which:
options: A substance only changes its state
A substance changes into an entirely new substance
mcqs.why: In a chemical reaction the atoms of the reactants are rearranged to form new substances with different composition and properties; the atoms themselves are not destroyed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a sign that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: Evolution of a gas with fizzing
mcqs.why: Gas evolution, precipitate formation, colour change and temperature change are signs of a chemical reaction. Melting, dissolving and cutting are physical changes with no new substance.

mcqs.q: Which metal, when ignited in air, burns with a dazzling white light?
mcqs.why: A magnesium ribbon burns in air with an intense, dazzling white light and leaves white ash of magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO.

mcqs.q: Iron reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce:
mcqs.why: The balanced reaction is Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2. The metal displaces hydrogen from the acid, forming iron chloride (the salt) and hydrogen gas.

mcqs.q: Carbon dioxide reacts with water to form:
mcqs.why: CO2 + H2O → H2CO3, carbonic acid. With sunlight and chlorophyll this same pairing of reactants is the basis of photosynthesis in green plants.

mcqs.q: In a chemical equation, the products are written:
mcqs.why: By convention reactants are written on the left of the arrow and the products formed are written on the right, showing that reactants change into products.

mcqs.q: A chemical equation represents a reaction using:
mcqs.why: A chemical equation uses symbols and formulae of substances together with signs such as (g), (s) and (l) to show physical states, for example CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(g).

lessons.title: Balancing Equations and Conservation of Mass
lessons.notes_html:
Law of Conservation of Mass

The law of conservation of mass states that during a chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants is equal to the total mass of the products. Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; the atoms are only rearranged.

Balanced and Unbalanced Equations

A balanced chemical equation has the number of atoms of each element equal on both sides, for example 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. An unbalanced equation, also called a skeleton equation, has unequal atoms of some element, for example Mg + O2 → MgO, where oxygen is 2 on the left and 1 on the right. Using coefficients to equalize the atoms is called balancing.

Worked Balancings

  • 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl
  • 2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3
  • 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3
  • Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2
  • 2NaBr + Cl2 → 2NaCl + Br2
  • Ca(HCO3)2 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + 2CO2 + 2H2O
  • 2NH4OH + H2SO4 → (NH4)2SO4 + 2H2O
  • 2CO + O2 → 2CO2, so in xCO + yO2 → zCO2, x = 2, y = 1, z = 2

Counting Atoms

In one molecule of Mg(HCO3)2, the subscript 2 outside the bracket doubles everything inside: HCO3 contains 3 oxygen atoms, so the molecule has 2 × 3 = 6 oxygen atoms. Photosynthesis, 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, shows conservation clearly: carbon 6, hydrogen 12 and oxygen 18 on both sides. When coal burns, the ash weighs less than the coal because most of the carbon escapes as carbon dioxide gas; counting the gas restores the balance.

Key Points

  • Total mass of reactants = total mass of products in every reaction.
  • A balanced equation has equal atoms of each element on both sides.
  • An unbalanced equation is also called a skeleton equation.
  • Only coefficients are changed when balancing — never the formulae.
  • Mg(HCO3)2 contains 6 oxygen atoms in one molecule.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an unbalanced chemical equation?
mcqs.why: In Na + Cl2 → NaCl, chlorine is 2 atoms on the left but only 1 on the right, so the equation is unbalanced. Its balanced form is 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl. The book key is correct.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a balanced chemical equation?
mcqs.why: Count the atoms: left side Fe = 2, Cl = 6; right side 2FeCl3 gives Fe = 2, Cl = 6. Only this option has equal atoms of every element on both sides.

mcqs.q: The equation xCO(g) + yO2(g) → zCO2(g) is properly balanced when:
mcqs.why: With x = 2, y = 1, z = 2: carbon is 2 on both sides, and oxygen is 2 + 2 = 4 on the left and 2 × 2 = 4 on the right, so the equation balances.

mcqs.q: How many oxygen atoms are present in one molecule of Mg(HCO3)2?
mcqs.why: The subscript 2 outside the bracket doubles the HCO3 group. Each group has 3 oxygen atoms, so one molecule has 2 × 3 = 6 oxygen atoms. The book key is correct.

mcqs.q: The law of conservation of mass states that in a chemical reaction:
options: Mass of reactants equals mass of products
Mass of products is always greater
mcqs.why: Mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; the atoms are only rearranged, so the total mass before and after the reaction stays the same.

mcqs.q: An unbalanced chemical equation is also called a:
mcqs.why: When the atoms of some element are unequal on the two sides, as in Mg + O2 → MgO, the equation is called a skeleton (unbalanced) equation.

mcqs.q: The correctly balanced equation for zinc with hydrochloric acid is:
mcqs.why: ZnCl2 needs 2 chlorine atoms, so 2HCl is required on the left. Then hydrogen is 2 on the left and H2 gives 2 on the right, so every element balances.

mcqs.q: To balance Fe + O2 → Fe2O3, the correct coefficients are:
mcqs.why: Fe2O3 has 3 oxygen atoms, so take 2Fe2O3 (6 oxygen atoms) and 3O2 on the left. Iron then needs 4 atoms on the left to match 2 × 2 = 4 on the right.

mcqs.q: The mass of ash left after burning coal is less than the mass of coal because:
options: The carbon escapes as carbon dioxide gas
mcqs.why: Coal is mostly carbon, which forms CO2 gas that escapes into the air. Only the non-combustible mineral matter remains as ash. Counting the gas, total mass is still conserved.

mcqs.q: In photosynthesis, 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, the number of oxygen atoms on each side is:
mcqs.why: Left side: 12 oxygen atoms from 6CO2 plus 6 from 6H2O = 18. Right side: 6 in glucose plus 12 in 6O2 = 18. Equal atoms show mass is conserved.

lessons.title: Types of Chemical Reactions
lessons.notes_html:
Combination (Addition) Reactions

In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form one compound: A + B → AB. Examples: C + O2 → CO2; CaO + CO2 → CaCO3; Fe + S → FeS; N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3; 2CO + O2 → 2CO2.

Decomposition Reactions

In a decomposition reaction, one compound splits up into two or more simple substances: AB → A + B. Examples: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 on heating; 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2 on heating, which produces oxygen gas.

Opposite of Each Other
