Disadvantages are limited backup time, costly batteries that must be replaced, extra electricity used in charging, and harm from old batteries if they are not disposed of properly.

Energy Conversions

  • UPS during charging: electrical energy changes into chemical energy in the battery.
  • UPS during use: chemical energy changes into electrical energy, and the inverter converts DC into AC.
  • Wind turbine: kinetic energy of wind changes into mechanical energy and then electrical energy.
  • Electric motor: electrical energy changes into mechanical energy.
  • Solar cooker: light and heat energy of the Sun change into heat energy in the food.

Wind Turbine and Solar Cooker

A wind turbine converts the kinetic energy of moving wind into electricity. The wind turns the fan blades, which rotate the shaft of the generator, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy.

A concave mirror is used in a solar cooker. It is a spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inward, like the inner side of a spoon. It converges light rays to a focus. In the cooker, parallel rays of sunlight are reflected and concentrated at the focus where a black cooking pot is placed, so enough heat is produced to cook food using free and clean solar energy.

Key Points

  • UPS means Uninterruptible Power Supply and it uses an inverter.
  • An inverter converts battery DC into AC for home appliances.
  • A wind turbine converts kinetic energy of wind into electricity.
  • A solar cooker uses a concave mirror to concentrate sunlight.

mcqs.q: Which mirror is used in a solar cooker?
mcqs.why: A concave mirror converges parallel sunlight to its focus, concentrating heat where the cooking pot is placed.

mcqs.q: Which device is used in a UPS?
mcqs.why: A UPS contains a battery and an inverter that converts stored DC power into AC for appliances during a failure.

mcqs.q: What does UPS stand for?
mcqs.why: UPS stands for Uninterruptible Power Supply because it supplies power immediately without interruption when mains fail.

mcqs.q: What does a DC to AC inverter do?
options: It stores chemical energy in a battery
It converts direct current into alternating current
It converts wind energy into electricity
It changes AC into heat only
mcqs.why: Batteries supply DC, but home appliances need AC, so the inverter converts battery DC into usable AC.

mcqs.q: Which energy is converted into electricity by a wind turbine?
mcqs.why: Moving wind turns the blades and generator shaft, so its kinetic energy is converted into electrical energy.

mcqs.q: What is a concave mirror?
options: A mirror curved outward like a ball
A flat mirror with no curve
A mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inward
mcqs.why: A concave mirror curves inward like the inner side of a spoon and converges light rays to a focus.

mcqs.q: During charging, a UPS converts electrical energy into:
options: Chemical energy stored in the battery
mcqs.why: While charging, mains electrical energy is stored as chemical energy in the UPS battery for later use.

mcqs.q: In a solar cooker, solar energy is finally converted into:
mcqs.why: The concave mirror concentrates sunlight at the pot, so light and heat energy of the Sun become heat that cooks the food.

mcqs.q: Which is a disadvantage of UPS technology?
options: It gives instant power in load-shedding
It protects computers from data loss
Batteries have limited backup time and must be replaced
mcqs.why: UPS batteries run for a limited time, cost money to replace, and old batteries can harm the environment if dumped carelessly.

mcqs.q: An electric motor converts electrical energy into:
mcqs.why: An electric motor changes electrical energy into mechanical rotational energy, as listed in the energy conversions of the unit.

lessons.title: Stars: Birth, Life and Death
lessons.notes_html:
Birth of a Star

A star is born in a nebula, a huge cloud of gas, mostly hydrogen, and dust. Gravity pulls the gas together, it becomes hotter and denser, and when the temperature becomes high enough, nuclear fusion starts and the star begins to shine.

Colour, Temperature and Brightness

The colour of a star shows its temperature. The hottest stars are blue, while cooler stars appear red or yellow. The surface temperature of the Sun is about 6000 degrees C. Bright stars may appear dim if they are far away from Earth, because apparent brightness depends on distance as well as real brightness.

Death of a Star

When the fuel of a star finishes, it dies. A medium star like the Sun expands into a red giant and then shrinks into a white dwarf. A massive star becomes a super giant, explodes as a supernova, and leaves behind a neutron star or a black hole. The last stage in the life of a massive star is a black hole.

Neutron Stars and Black Holes

A neutron star forms when the core left after a supernova collapses under gravity with such great pressure that protons and electrons combine to form neutrons. It is extremely small and incredibly dense. A spoonful of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

A black hole is so dense that its gravity is strong enough that not even light can escape from it. It cannot be seen directly by any telescope, because no light comes out of it. Scientists detect it indirectly by its effects on nearby stars and matter falling into it.

Key Points

  • Stars are born in a nebula when fusion starts in hot dense gas.
  • Blue stars are the hottest, and the Sun surface is about 6000 degrees C.
  • Medium stars end as white dwarfs after a red giant stage.
  • Massive stars end through a supernova as a neutron star or black hole.

mcqs.q: The colour of the hottest star is:
mcqs.why: Star colour indicates temperature, and blue stars are the hottest while red stars are the coolest.

mcqs.q: Surface temperature of the Sun is:
mcqs.why: The book gives the surface temperature of the Sun as about 6000 degrees C; the much higher value belongs to its centre.

mcqs.q: The last stage in the life of a massive star is:
mcqs.why: A massive star passes through a super giant and supernova stage, and its collapsed core can end as a black hole.

mcqs.q: Bright stars may appear dim because they are:
mcqs.why: Apparent brightness decreases with distance, so an actually bright star can look dim when it is very far from Earth.

mcqs.q: A star is born in a nebula when which process starts?
options: Nuclear fusion in hot dense gas
mcqs.why: Gravity compresses gas in a nebula until it is hot enough for nuclear fusion, and then the star begins to shine.

mcqs.q: A medium star like the Sun ends its life as a:
options: White dwarf after a red giant stage
mcqs.why: Medium stars expand into red giants and then shrink into white dwarfs when their fuel finishes.

mcqs.q: How is a neutron star formed?
options: By cooling of a white dwarf in space
By collapse of a supernova core where protons and electrons form neutrons
By joining of two planets together
By expansion of a red giant
mcqs.why: After a supernova the remaining core collapses so strongly that protons and electrons combine into neutrons, forming a neutron star.

mcqs.q: Why can a black hole not be seen directly by any telescope?
options: It is too small to magnify
No light can escape from it to reach the telescope
It is hidden behind the Sun always
It gives out only radio waves
mcqs.why: Telescopes collect light from objects, but a black hole traps even light, so it is detected only by effects on nearby matter.

mcqs.q: A spoonful of neutron star material would be remarkable because it would:
options: Weigh about a billion tons on Earth
mcqs.why: A neutron star is incredibly dense, so even a spoonful of its material would have a mass of about a billion tons.

mcqs.q: A massive star explodes at the end of its life as a:
mcqs.why: When a massive star becomes a super giant and its fuel ends, it explodes violently as a supernova.

lessons.title: Galaxies and Our Solar System
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Galaxy

A galaxy is a huge collection of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity. A galaxy may contain billions of stars. Our Sun belongs to the Milky Way galaxy, and our Solar System is a part of the Milky Way galaxy.

Types of Galaxies

  • Spiral galaxies, like our Milky Way.
  • Elliptical galaxies.
  • Irregular galaxies.

Distances in Space

Distances of stars are measured in light years, because kilometres and miles are far too small for such huge distances. The nearest star after the Sun is Proxima Centauri. Even this nearest star is so far that its light takes years to reach us, which is why light years are used.

Key Points

  • A galaxy is a huge system of stars, gas and dust held by gravity.
  • Galaxies are spiral, elliptical or irregular in type.
  • Our Solar System belongs to the Milky Way galaxy.
  • Star distances are measured in light years, and Proxima Centauri is nearest after the Sun.

mcqs.q: Distances of stars are measured in:
mcqs.why: Stellar distances are enormous, so astronomers use light years, the distance light travels in one year, instead of small units.

mcqs.q: Our Solar System is a part of:
mcqs.why: The Sun and its Solar System belong to the Milky Way, which is a spiral galaxy containing billions of stars.

mcqs.q: The nearest star after the Sun is:
mcqs.why: Proxima Centauri is the closest star to us after the Sun, though even its light takes over four years to arrive.

mcqs.q: A galaxy is best described as:
options: A single star with planets around it
A huge collection of stars, gas and dust held by gravity
A cloud of gas where one star is born
A vehicle used to carry satellites
mcqs.why: A galaxy contains billions of stars together with gas and dust, all bound together by gravity into one huge system.

mcqs.q: Which are the main types of galaxies?
mcqs.why: Galaxies are classified by shape into spiral galaxies like the Milky Way, elliptical galaxies and irregular galaxies.

mcqs.q: The Milky Way galaxy is of which type?
mcqs.why: Our Milky Way is given in the book as an example of a spiral galaxy, with stars arranged in spiral arms.

mcqs.q: About how many stars may a galaxy contain?
options: Only the Sun and eight planets
mcqs.why: A galaxy is a vast system that may contain billions of stars along with huge amounts of gas and dust.

mcqs.q: What holds the stars, gas and dust of a galaxy together?
mcqs.why: Gravity binds the stars, gas and dust of a galaxy together and keeps the whole system from flying apart.

mcqs.q: Why are light years used instead of kilometres for star distances?
options: Kilometres cannot be measured at night
Star distances are too huge for small units
Light years are shorter than kilometres
Stars move at the speed of light
mcqs.why: Even the nearest star is trillions of kilometres away, so the light year is a practical unit for such distances.

mcqs.q: Our Sun belongs to which galaxy?
mcqs.why: The book states that our Sun belongs to the Milky Way galaxy, so the whole Solar System is part of it.

lessons.title: Telescopes on Earth and in Space
lessons.notes_html:
The Telescope

A telescope is an instrument that helps in seeing heavenly objects. It is the device that makes far away objects appear closer and bigger, so their details can be seen and studied. Through a telescope the craters of the Moon can be seen clearly, Jupiter appears as a bright disc with its four large moons, and Saturn is seen with its beautiful rings.

Optical and Radio Telescopes

An optical telescope collects visible light from heavenly objects and forms their images with lenses or mirrors, so it is used at night in clear weather. A radio telescope collects invisible radio waves with a large dish antenna. It can work day and night and in all weather, and it detects objects that give out little or no visible light.

Problem With Telescopes on Earth

A telescope on Earth suffers from the defect that light coming from the stars has to pass through the atmosphere. The moving air blurs the images, and clouds, weather, light pollution and the day-night cycle also limit observations. The atmosphere also absorbs ultraviolet and infrared radiations.

Advantages of Space Telescopes

A telescope placed in space, like the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope, is above the atmosphere. Its images are sharp and clear, it can observe continuously at all times, there is no light pollution, and it can detect radiations which the atmosphere blocks. Hence space telescopes give far better and deeper views of the universe than Earth-based telescopes.

Key Points

  • A telescope makes distant heavenly objects appear closer and clearer.
  • Optical telescopes collect visible light, radio telescopes collect radio waves.
  • Earth telescopes suffer because starlight must pass through the atmosphere.
  • Space telescopes give sharp images free from weather and light pollution.

mcqs.q: An instrument that helps in seeing heavenly objects is a:
mcqs.why: A telescope collects light from distant heavenly bodies and makes them appear closer and bigger for detailed study.

mcqs.q: A telescope on Earth suffers from the defect that light from stars has to pass through:
mcqs.why: Starlight is blurred while passing through the moving air of the atmosphere, which limits ground-based telescopes.

mcqs.q: What is the device that makes far away objects appear closer to see their detail?
mcqs.why: The telescope magnifies distant stars and planets so their details can be seen and studied by astronomers.

mcqs.q: What is the main difference between an optical telescope and a radio telescope?
options: Optical collects visible light, radio collects radio waves
Optical works in daytime, radio only at night
Radio forms images with small lenses only
Optical detects objects with no light at all
mcqs.why: Optical telescopes use lenses or mirrors for visible light, while radio telescopes use a dish for invisible radio waves.

mcqs.q: A radio telescope has the advantage that it can work:
options: Day and night and in all weather
mcqs.why: Radio waves are not blocked by daylight or clouds in the same way, so radio telescopes observe at any time.

mcqs.q: What is the advantage of putting a telescope in space?
options: It becomes cheaper to repair daily
Images are not blurred by the atmosphere
It can use sunlight as fuel
mcqs.why: Above the atmosphere there is no blurring, weather or light pollution, so space telescopes give clear detailed images.

mcqs.q: Space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb can also detect:
options: Only visible light from the Moon
Ultraviolet and infrared radiations blocked by the atmosphere
mcqs.why: The atmosphere absorbs ultraviolet and infrared rays, but space telescopes above it can receive these radiations.

mcqs.q: Through a telescope, Saturn is best recognised by its:
options: Four large moons in a line
mcqs.why: The model observation in the book describes Saturn seen with its beautiful rings, far clearer than with the naked eye.

mcqs.q: Through a telescope, Jupiter appears as:
options: A disc with its four large moons in a line
A ringed planet with no moons
A red point of light only
A galaxy of billions of stars
mcqs.why: The telescopic view described in the book shows Jupiter as a bright disc with four large moons arranged in a line.

mcqs.q: Why can space telescopes observe continuously?
options: They are not affected by clouds, weather or the day-night cycle
They move faster than Earth telescopes
They use bigger batteries than rockets
They are placed on the Moon surface
mcqs.why: In orbit above the atmosphere, observing is not interrupted by clouds, bad weather or daylight in the same way.

lessons.title: Space Exploration and Its Benefits
lessons.notes_html:
Rockets, Probes and Space Stations

A rocket is a vehicle designed to carry an artificial satellite into outer space. A space probe is an unmanned robotic spacecraft sent to explore outer space and other planets and to send information back to Earth. Examples are Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, and other well-known probes like Pioneer and Cassini.

A space station is a large artificial satellite in orbit around the Earth where astronauts can live and work for long periods, such as the International Space Station. There, scientists perform experiments in weightlessness which cannot be done on Earth, study effects of space on the human body, and observe the Earth and the universe.

GPS and Benefits of Space Technology

GPS stands for Global Positioning System. It helps a receiver, mobile phone or navigator catch signals from satellites to find exact location and directions. Space exploration technology has given weather forecasting, navigation and communication satellites, methods to locate minerals, fossil fuels and underground water, improvements in health and medicine, television and mobile networks, and disaster warnings for storms and floods.

Problems Faced by Astronauts

Astronauts face weightlessness that weakens muscles and bones, no air to breathe, extreme temperatures, harmful radiations, loneliness and limited food, water and oxygen. They overcome these with space suits providing oxygen, pressure and temperature control, regular exercise, stored supplies, protective shielding and constant contact with mission control.

A gravity-free environment is achieved when a spacecraft is in free fall in orbit around the Earth. The spacecraft and everything inside fall together with the same acceleration, so the occupants feel weightless. Spending on space exploration is an investment, not mere extravagance, because its technologies save lives and serve everyone daily, though spending should stay balanced with needs on Earth.

Key Points

  • A rocket carries artificial satellites into outer space.
  • Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are famous unmanned space probes.
  • GPS means Global Positioning System and works through satellites.
  • Space stations allow long stays and experiments in weightlessness.

mcqs.q: A vehicle designed to carry an artificial satellite in outer space is a:
mcqs.why: Only a rocket provides the powerful thrust needed to lift an artificial satellite out of the atmosphere into outer space.

mcqs.q: What does GPS stand for?
mcqs.why: GPS stands for Global Positioning System, which uses satellite signals to find exact location and directions.

mcqs.q: What is a space probe?
options: An unmanned robotic spacecraft sent to explore space
A telescope placed on a mountain
A rocket fuel tank in orbit
mcqs.why: A space probe carries no crew; it explores planets and deep space and sends information back to Earth.

mcqs.q: Which pair names two well-known space probes?
mcqs.why: Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are the famous unmanned probes given in the book, along with Pioneer and Cassini.

mcqs.q: What is a space station?
options: A rocket launching pad on Earth
A radio telescope dish in a desert
A large artificial satellite where astronauts live and work in orbit
A probe sent to another planet
mcqs.why: A space station like the ISS stays in Earth orbit so astronauts can live, work and do experiments for long periods.

mcqs.q: Experiments in a space station use its special environment of:
mcqs.why: In orbit everything falls together, giving a gravity-free environment where special experiments and manufacturing are possible.

mcqs.q: Which is a benefit generated by space exploration technology?
mcqs.why: Weather satellites, GPS, communication links and disaster warnings are direct daily benefits of space technology.

mcqs.q: How do astronauts overcome the problem of no air and extreme temperatures in space?
options: By wearing space suits with oxygen, pressure and temperature control
mcqs.why: Specially designed space suits supply oxygen and maintain safe pressure and temperature for astronauts outside the craft.

mcqs.q: A gravity-free environment in orbit is achieved when a spacecraft is:
options: In free fall around the Earth with everything inside falling together
mcqs.why: The craft and its occupants fall towards Earth with the same acceleration, so they float and feel weightless.

mcqs.q: The best comment on huge spending on space exploration is that it is:
options: An investment whose technologies benefit daily life
Useful only for astronauts in orbit
A waste because satellites are unused
mcqs.why: Weather, GPS, communication, medical and resource technologies repay the cost, though spending should stay balanced.
